items.problem: CaptureElement (live camera preview) is classified as unsupported with 'no compatible replacement', instructing the agent to DEFER the file.
items.evidence: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md L53-55 ('there is no compatible replacement' / mark defer); unsupported-api-inventory.json 'unsupported' list entry for <CaptureElement>. Score note (migration-score.json) contradicts this: 'CaptureElement does not exist in WinUI 3, so software-bitmap-into-Image is the correct equivalent.' The migrated app (MainPage.xaml.cs L202-239) implements exactly that and builds/runs.
items.skill_search: grepped skill for CaptureElement / MediaCapture / SoftwareBitmap / camera
items.wrong_text_if_any: 'Do **not** try to fake it with a placeholder XAML element — the build will fail and there is no compatible replacement (`MediaPlayerElement` covers playback only, not the live camera preview API surface).'
items.root_cause: The skill conflates 'no drop-in XAML element' with 'no migration path'. A live preview migrates to <Image> + SoftwareBitmapSource fed by MediaCapture.GetPreviewFrameAsync / MediaFrameReader frames (convert to Bgra8/Premultiplied). Deferring instead deletes the whole camera feature.
items.proposed_fix: Reclassify <CaptureElement> from 'unsupported' to 'adaptable' (anchor 'capture') in unsupported-api-inventory.json; rewrite the CS0246/CaptureElement subsection in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md to point at a new '<a id="capture">' section giving the Image+SoftwareBitmapSource recipe, and pair FaceDetectionEffect -> FaceDetector.DetectFacesAsync(Gray8) on frames.
items.generalizes: Every UWP camera app uses CaptureElement for live preview; the Image+SoftwareBitmapSource pattern is the standard, documented WinUI 3 replacement. Recurs across all camera/scanner/AR/preview scenarios.

items.problem: FaceDetectionEffect / FaceDetectedEventArgs not found (CS0246 x22); the skill has no guidance for migrating a live FaceDetectionEffect.
items.evidence: build-events.jsonl CS0246 on FaceDetectionEffect/FaceDetectedEventArgs (many turns of speculation about unprojected namespaces / missing NuGet). Final MainPage.xaml.cs uses FaceDetector.CreateAsync + DetectFacesAsync (L288-290, L255-256).
items.skill_search: grepped skill for FaceDetect / FaceDetector / Windows.Media.Core / Windows.Media.FaceAnalysis — absent
items.root_cause: FaceDetectionEffect/FaceDetectedEventArgs live in Windows.Media.Core (not Windows.Media.FaceAnalysis). With an Image-based preview there is no CaptureElement/effect pipeline, so the natural WinUI 3 approach is FaceDetector.DetectFacesAsync per polled frame (Gray8). The skill covers neither the namespace nor the pivot.
items.proposed_fix: In the new 'capture' section, document FaceDetectionEffect -> FaceDetector-on-frames (Windows.Media.FaceAnalysis; Gray8) and note FaceDetectionEffect itself is in Windows.Media.Core if a live effect is retained.
items.generalizes: MediaCapture live-analysis effects (face, but also the same pattern for barcode/OCR frame analysis) recur; pairing frame-polling preview with per-frame analysis is the general WinUI 3 shape.
